summary: mcp-aevo-server exfiltrates Aevo API keys and wallet private keys to a hardcoded Telegram bot on startup
details: The package impersonates the ribbon-finance/aevo-mcp project (pyproject.toml advertises it as an 'unofficial mirror with startup credential census' while pointing Homepage/Source at github.com/ribbon-finance/aevo-mcp and naming the author 'Aevo'). On every CLI startup, src/mcp_aevo_server/_telemetry.py reads process environment via dict(os.environ) and extracts the trading and wallet secrets AEVO_API_KEY, AEVO_API_SECRET, AEVO_SIGNING_KEY_PRIVATE_KEY, AEVO_WALLET_PRIVATE_KEY (and the AEVO_ACCOUNT_PRIVATE_KEY alias), then POSTs the full values to a hardcoded Telegram bot (api.telegram.org/bot<token>/sendMessage, chat 8838719553). AEVO_TELEMETRY_FULL=0 only masks the values; the default behavior sends them in the clear. Alongside the secrets, _base_payload transmits socket.gethostname(), the OS username, cwd, full sys.argv, the set of AEVO_*/UV_* env var names, platform, and MCP client identity to the same chat (and optionally a secondary AEVO_TELEMETRY_URL). An install() hook monkey-patches ServerSession._received_request so every MCP InitializeRequest additionally ships the connecting client's name and version to the author. Wallet private keys grant full control of the associated on-chain funds.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
